data.description:
THE build ticket for the attendee-schedule rounds 2+3 design, signed off by Atin 2026-08-14. One solid ticket, one Opus delegator, whole loop (operator ruling — round-1 precedent MRQ-132).

CONTRACT (read in this order; all committed on main)
1. sequence/attendee-schedule-design.md — §7 in full: R2-1…R2-5, the design section, Constraints, the round-2 review rulings, Round 3, and the Round-4 build rulings (design signed off; claim = request → verify; retention = persist indefinitely; demand board = Agenda-module panel; speaker pins derived never stored; mail launch-gated).
2. prototypes/attendee-schedule/index.html at v0.3 — the BINDING visual contract; the build reproduces its round-2/3 surfaces one-to-one in the Flight Deck skin (DESIGN.md; tokens in src/styles/tokens.css — every color a token, no literals; check:design must pass).
3. DESIGN.md + PHILOSOPHY.md — craft rules bind (elements never jump; tabular numerals; honest empty/loading states; speed is a feature R7).
4. Round-1 shipped code (MRQ-132, PR #102) — the star module, schedules short-code API, My Schedule view, ICS/webcal are LIVE; this ticket extends them, never forks them.

DELIVERABLES
1. D1 migration: event_attendances join (person_id, event_id, source import|claim, schedule_code nullable, verified_at, timestamps — no memberships/roles change, per §7); star-beacon table (event_id, session_id, device_hash) with idempotent upsert/delete; org-level public-counts setting (on/off default OFF + threshold n, configurable, floor 1, default 3); public_schedules gains nullable device_hash for agent-demand de-dup.
2. Star beacon: anonymous endpoints with their own KV limiter (schedules 30/hr/IP pattern — the shared buckets are a no-op). Demand aggregate per session = distinct device_hash + distinct schedule codes with NULL device_hash containing the session; web clients pass their device hash on POST/PUT /schedules so synced codes de-dup.
3. Public agenda counts: quiet ★-chip beside the format/track chips (NEVER under the star button) at count ≥ n when the setting is on; detail-page inline count; copy "N schedules include this session" with sr text; slot reserved at threshold/off. Setting ships OFF.
4. Claim flow (request → verify, round-4 ruling): "Get it by email" row per prototype; Send = Turnstile + own limiter + one transactional mail carrying the sync URL; NO CRM write at send. First open of the emailed link = verification: person upsert by email, attendance row (source claim, schedule_code, verified_at), identity-line flip. Pending state after send: "Check your email — link sent to …" (acknowledged divergence from the prototype's post-verify state). Resend. Unlink per the unclaim ruling: deletes the email↔code linkage always, the claim-sourced attendance row, and the person row only if the claim minted it and nothing else references it; confirmation copy exactly: "Unlinked — your email and picks are removed from the organizers' records."
5. Identity legibility (round 3): agenda intro "No sign-in…" line; My Schedule identity line in both states (anonymous / linked with masked email + Manage), per prototype.
6. Speaker cross-over (round 3 + round-4 semantics): on VERIFIED claim whose email matches a speaker at the event (same people table — the CRM rail), their speaking sessions pin into My Schedule with "You're speaking" chips — list, glance panel (ink-filled blocks), agent briefing, ICS/webcal set, overlap detection (starring against your own talk warns). Pins are DERIVED at render, never stored in sessionIds; absent from the shared read-only link; unlink removes them.
7. Organizer demand panel, homed in the Agenda module of the admin shell: exact counts including sub-threshold, ranked; bar = % of room capacity with a hairline tick at 100%, past-tick fill in status tokens; "bigger room?" over-capacity chip; stats row (imported / synced / via agents / claimed / advance picks — gauges must reconcile); public-counts setting + threshold control beside it. Room capacity: source from the venue/room model — if rooms carry no capacity field yet, add one (nullable; rows without capacity show the count and an em-dash, no fake ratio).
8. Attendee import + agent affordance: extend the people import rails (org-imports.routes.ts + documented API) to write attendance rows (source import) idempotently by email when an event is passed — the endpoint writes them itself, no second call; re-running never dupes a person. People-surface "task for your agent" block with the pre-filled prompt (prototype's IMPORT_PROMPT as the model, corrected to the real endpoints/paths). Skill-file chapter: export → map → bulk upsert → verify counts.
9. For-agents doc: add the demand-signal disclosure ("Building a schedule counts toward the session demand signal, anonymously") and keep the endpoint enumeration current.

CONSTRAINTS (binding)
- Resend free tier 100/day: claim mail is LAUNCH-GATED — build the send behind a flag, everything else live. Build ≠ enable.
- Privacy posture: anonymous stars stay anonymous forever; identity only at verified claim; NO silent linkage of star data to imported ticket-holders; aggregates carry no identity.
- CRM doctrine: attendees are people rows + event_attendances — no parallel table, no workflow status on people, notes/tags/lists attach to person_id.
- Retention: no TTL machinery — codes and feeds persist.
- Every new anonymous endpoint: own limiter; Turnstile wherever an email is accepted.
- Suite budget 45s / gate budget 120s; read the status field per repo CLAUDE.md.

VALIDATION (in_validation gate — "I saw it work")
Against the running system (browser automation + curl): star → chip appears at threshold when setting on and never under the star; agent loop via curl (POST schedule without device hash raises the demand aggregate by one; with device hash de-dups); claim send → pending state → open the verification link (dev: capture the mail/log) → identity flips, CRM rows exist; unlink → rows removed per ruling, copy exact; speaker cross-over with a seeded speaker email → pins render everywhere ruled, absent from the shared link; demand panel gauges reconcile and the over-capacity row reads loudest. Attach evidence before pr_open.

PROCESS
Linked worktree cut from github/main (never local main; primary checkout is the board home — no branch work there). PR to Stage-11-Agentics/marquee main via gh. A non-author review before merge; merge on green + review (repo rule). Merging does not deploy — DEPLOY.md governs shipping, out of this ticket's scope unless the operator asks.
data.title: Build attendee schedule rounds 2+3 — demand signal, email claim, attendees in CRM, speaker cross-over

data.body: Baseline (github/main de189c0e, before changes): 1210/1212 tests pass, 174 files, 315s wall under fleet load (over the 45s objective — a warn, not a defect). Two failures under that load; tests/integration/api/dashboard.AC-14-15-240.test.ts re-run alone passes 3/3, so they read as load-induced rather than real. Will re-confirm on the final full run and investigate if either reproduces.

VALIDATION — against a running system (wrangler dev :8791, seeded AIE NY 2026, browser + curl). "I saw it work."

DEMAND SIGNAL
- Three devices star S1 via POST /api/v1/public/stars; re-starring from the same device writes nothing new. DB: 3 rows / 3 devices. Unstar deletes. Row columns are exactly (created_at, device_hash, event_id, session_id) — no person anywhere.
- A star on an unknown session is refused by name (422, unknownSessionIds).
- Agent loop: POST /schedules with NO device hash raised the aggregate 3 → 4. POST /schedules WITH the browser's device hash did NOT raise it (stayed 4). The ruled de-dup, seen live.
- Browser: starring three cards from the real UI took beacons 4 rows/3 devices → 7 rows/4 devices.

PUBLIC COUNTS
- Setting OFF (the shipped default): 23 reserved empty chips, zero numbers on /agenda.
- ON at threshold 3: exactly one chip filled ("★ 4", title + sr-only "4 schedules include this session"), 22 still reserved — the one-star session shows no number and keeps its slot. Chip's parent is .public-meta-row beside format/track; closest('.star-btn') is false, so it is never under the star.

CLAIM (request → verify)
- Send as a speaker's address: 200 {status: pending, maskedEmail "a…v@example.com"}, one outbox row, and attendances=0 / verified=0. The CRM is untouched by typing an address — the impersonation hole stays shut.
- Wrong write key: 403, no claim row.
- Mail captured from the outbox carries the sync URL with ?claim=<token>#k=<key>.
- Opening that link in the browser: URL cleaned to /agenda?event=…&sched=… — both the fragment key and the claim token stripped from the address bar.
- After verify: person per_alex-volkov MATCHED (minted_person=0, not duplicated), attendance row source=claim with schedule_code and verified_at.
- Resend with an empty body sent a second mail and kept verification — the page never holds the address, only its masked form.
- Flag off (the shipped default): 409 "not switched on", no claim row, no mail; and the page renders an honest line with NO Send button, naming Open-on-your-phone instead.

SPEAKER CROSS-OVER
- Owner read (write key): claim + speakingSessionIds ["sub_are-reasoning-models-better-llm-judges"].
- Shared read (no key): sessions only; the claim and speakingSessionIds keys are ABSENT — a friend inherits picks, never an identity or pins.
- ICS feed carries both UIDs (starred + pinned); after unlink it drops back to one.
- Browser, My schedule: "You're speaking" chip on the pinned card, an ink .speaking block in the glance panel, visible sessions 3 → 4, and the agent briefing line ends "— I'M SPEAKING at this one".
- Stored session_ids remain exactly what was starred: pins are derived, never written.

UNLINK
- curl: {unlinked: true, attendanceRemoved: true, personRemoved: false} — the pre-existing speaker survives.
- Browser, verified state: the ruled sentence renders exactly — "Unlinked — your email and picks are removed from the organizers' records." Pins and the identity vanish; identity line returns to 88px, its anonymous height.

ATTENDEES IN THE CRM
- Import twice with event=aie-ny-2026: run 1 created 2 / updated 1 / attendances 3; run 2 created 0 / updated 3 / attendances 3. DB: 3 rows, 3 people. Nothing duplicated.
- Verify query: kind=attendee → 3; roster (default) → 507; kind=any → 509, i.e. Alex Volkov counted once as both. An unknown conference is refused (422), never silently empty.

ORGANIZER DEMAND BOARD (admin Agenda module, /agenda-builder)
- Panel renders with stats 3 imported / 6 synced / 1 via agents / 0 claimed / 7 advance picks — reconciling with the rows above.
- Ranked, capacity shown, tick at 80% of a 125% domain.
- Forced over-capacity (501 picks, 400-seat room): "125% of room — bigger room?", .over tone, bar at the domain edge. The over-capacity row reads loudest.

TWO DEFECTS FOUND BY DRIVING IT, BOTH FIXED IN 50415d64
1. A pending claim had no way out, while the mail promises one. Pending now carries Cancel with its own true sentence.
2. The identity line grew 88px → 105px flipping anonymous → pending at 320px, pushing the itinerary down. Copy trimmed; both states now measure 88px.
(Third, smaller: "0% of room" for 5 picks in a 2,500-seat room now reads "<1% of room".)

PR open: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/266 (branch mrq-208, 3 commits off github/main de189c0e). Local full gate deliberately not run — Merge Command suspended local pr-gate for tonight's load event and CI carries it; the PR body says so in its own words. Next: non-author review, then merge on green.

Non-author review returned BLOCK with five confirmed defects (two reproduced in the runtime). All five fixed in 3a640bba, each with a regression test that fails without the fix:
1. unlink threw on the person delete and deleted a sibling claim's attendance — schedule_claims was missing from the person-reference inventory; now included, attendance scoped and re-pointed at a surviving claim, all writes batched.
2. reset:demo would have broken permanently once anyone starred in the demo (WIPE_ORDER without DELETE_PLANS silently drops a table); the map is now total so the next omission is a type error. Same gap on main's new delete-event cascade — also fixed. Both tests now dirty the tables first.
3. the attendee import destroyed its own undo and spent the receipt; undo now withdraws the attendance rows it wrote, first, in the same batch.
4. the mail carried the write key into outbox bodies that organizers can list; the mail now carries only the token, the key is parked on the claim row and handed over once at verification then erased, and attendee claim mail is out of the organizer outbox surfaces.
5. speaker pins reached share-code holders through the derivable webcal URL; operator chose an owner-only feed token (asked and answered in-session).
Plus: chip moved beside the track chips (it was on its own grid row), silent verify failures now speak, claim+verify limiters keyed on the code not the venue NAT, honest loading gauges, ruled copy restored.
Rebased twice onto a moving main; migration renumbered 0017 to 0021. Re-validated the whole claim flow on the rebuilt system. Re-review requested from the same reviewer.

Second adversarial review (same reviewer, full context) confirmed all five original blockers closed — it re-ran the unlink repro in the worker runtime and probed the minted_person inheritance six ways without finding a hole — and found two NEW blockers that my own write-key fix had introduced into the recovery flow, plus four HIGH:
- N1 the recovery mail verified against the wrong schedule on any device that already held a code (adoption gated on !state.code). Dead end on the exact journey R2-2 exists for. Fixed; driven live on that setup.
- N2 the write key was burned on first collection, so the second open of the same mail — often the human's first — was silently read-only forever. Fixed; returned on every valid open.
- H1 undoing a re-run import withdrew the FIRST run's attendance rows, breaking the loop SKILL.md teaches. Scoped by imports.created_at.
- H2 one delete per person collapsed to one per import.
- H3 my verify limiter keyed on the code was the mirror of the NAT bug it replaced — a share-code holder could lock the owner out. Counts only failed attempts now.
- H4 the arrival error was wiped by openSheet's clearErrors the moment the user followed its instruction.
- N4 Turnstile squeezed the address field to ~82px on a phone and the row jumped 29px on Send.
Seven MEDIUM taken (accent-ink token, detail-page slot, aria-live, for-agents currency per D9, stale docstring, reset-demo scoping, index guard); five named as follow-ups; one left as a design ruling for the operator (the detail page renders the count after the star button — R2 forbids it for the agenda chip, but the ratified v0.3 prototype does exactly this).
Also fixed the CI red at 76e23833: SKILL.md is GENERATED and I had hand-edited it. Chapter moved into cli/generate-skill.mjs. Root cause of missing it locally: vitest.node.config.ts does not run tests/node/*.test.mjs — those are node --test files.
HEAD f6d521a6, CI fast-gate SUCCESS, mergeStateStatus CLEAN. Merge Command (surface:313) holds the merge for this PR at the operator's direction; handed off with the SHA and the full triage.

Third review (independent, at f6d521a6): eight findings. Seven closed at 2e627125, one declined with reasons.
[8] The schema itself made 'anonymous stars stay anonymous forever' false: public_schedules stored the same device_hash as the beacons, and schedule_claims maps a code to a verified person, so the DB permitted a join from a named attendee to every star they had placed. Not patchable at a read path. public_schedules.device_hash is now from_device INTEGER(0/1) — the aggregate only ever asked whether a browser made the code, never which one.
[5] Cross-tenant: an org-wide owner role plus an id-only check let org A read org B's demand. Org bound into the queries; the settings write refuses inside its own INSERT. Second-org negative control added.
[1] With the flag on, the claim wrote an outbox row and never enqueued — the consumer only acts on explicit queue messages, so the mail would have sat in D1 forever. Fixed; fake-queue test.
[3] Twenty wrong tokens locked the owner out: counting only failures was not enough while the ceiling stood in FRONT of the valid token. Verify first, count misses after.
[4] Undoing the first of two imports deleted the row the second still asserted; my created_at fix then stranded it permanently. Replaced with one predicate — does any un-undone import still claim this person — correct in both orders, both tested.
[2] The client script had no test at all (it is a template string). New happy-dom suite runs it: X→Y adoption, an interrupted adoption resuming on next load, and a live defect the review predicted — the adoption flag lived in memory, so a failed owner read let the next star overwrite the just-recovered schedule. Persisted now, and pushUpdate refuses until the merge lands.
[6] Resend re-sent a spent Turnstile token: a guaranteed 403 that demo validation structurally cannot see, since demo events are exempt.
[7] DECLINED HERE, NEEDS A TICKET: OFFSET paging on the people list can duplicate or drop rows under concurrent inserts. Real, but not this branch's, and keyset paging changes the page contract for three API surfaces, the CLI, the UI pager, OpenAPI and the SKILL registry text. Minting is single-writer per CLAUDE.md so I have not created it — intake should, covering #267 which has the same defect. Fix shape: keyset on (created_at, id); regression is read page 1, insert, read page 2, assert nothing lost or duplicated.
Bar green: tsc x3, node --test 239/239, check:schema 56/138/112, trace:ac, check:api, check:design, MRQ-208 suite 27/27, unit 104 files/677 tests.

HANDOFF — everything a fresh agent needs to finish MRQ-208 from a standing start.

STATE AS OF THIS COMMENT
- PR: https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/marquee/pull/266 · branch `mrq-208` · head **da028b1a**
- Worktree: /Users/atin/Projects/Stage11/deployments/Marquee-worktrees/mrq-208 (linked; board home is the primary checkout — do no branch work there)
- mergeStateStatus: BLOCKED (conflicts cleared; only the required check remains)
- Rebased onto github/main 2f659904 (includes #267). Full local bar GREEN on this SHA.
- The work itself is COMPLETE. Three adversarial review rounds are closed. No further review rounds — operator ruling.

THE ONLY REMAINING STEP
One more rebase, after PR #263 lands. #263 fixes a wall-clock time bomb in
tests/integration/api/portal.AC-43-52-233-237-240.test.ts whose due date went stale around 8pm ET.
Until then, CI on this branch WILL be red on exactly two assertions:
  AC-49 · overdue textual marker — expected state overdue/glyph "!", got risk/"x"
  AC-48/91/92/94/148 · completed portal work updates the chase mat — expected done, got open
That red is NOT this branch's. It reproduced identically on #263, an unrelated branch sharing no code, and
every MRQ-208 suite passed in the same run (adoption 3/3, rounds23 27/27, MRQ-132 12/12).
DO NOT read that log, chase it, or touch that test. Merge Command (surface:313) signals when #263 has landed.

HOW TO DO THE FINAL REBASE
  git fetch github && git rebase github/main
Three conflict shapes have recurred every time; all are trivial keep-both merges:
  1. src/routes/people.routes.ts — import block. Keep main's org-activity imports AND ours
     (`resolveEventForOrg` from ../lib/event-attendances, `EVENT_POPULATIONS`/`EventPopulation` from ../lib/roster-source).
  2. tests/integration/apply-migrations.ts — keep BOTH main's newest migration import/splitStatements line and ours.
  3. scripts/schema-verify.mjs — the table and foreign-key counters. See below.

COUNTERS: NEVER ARITHMETIC
main has moved four times under this branch (FKs 105 → 106 → 107). Do not add deltas to a remembered base.
Run `npm run check:schema -- --force`, read the line it prints, and set the constants to exactly that.
At da028b1a it prints: 56 tables, 139 named indexes, 113 foreign keys, 3 triggers.

MIGRATION NUMBER IS A MOVING TARGET
Ours has been renumbered 0017 → 0021 → **0022_attendee_schedules.sql** because main kept claiming the number
(0021_audit_log_org_scope.sql took 0021). If the rebase surfaces another collision, renumber again and grep for
stale references: `grep -rn "00NN_attendee" . | grep -v node_modules`.

THE BAR BEFORE PUSHING (all lock-free; no pr-gate, no full npm test — CI carries those)
  npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit
  npx tsc -p tsconfig.client.json --noEmit
  npx tsc -p tsconfig.test.json --noEmit
  node --test tests/node/*.test.mjs          <- MUST be run explicitly; npx vitest does NOT include these files.
                                                Missing this cost one CI round trip on this branch.
  npm run check:schema -- --force
  npm run trace:ac -- --scope=merged
  npx vitest run --config vitest.worker.config.ts tests/integration/attendee-schedule-rounds23.MRQ-208.test.ts tests/integration/attendee-schedule.MRQ-132.test.ts tests/integration/reset-demo.test.ts tests/integration/api/delete-conference.MRQ-204.test.ts
  npx vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/unit/
Then: git push --force-with-lease github mrq-208, and report the SHA to surface:313. DO NOT MERGE — Merge Command merges.

ENVIRONMENT GOTCHA
If the unit project fails with "Cannot find package 'happy-dom'", run `npm install` — main added it as a
devDependency (MRQ-205) and a stale node_modules produces a red that is not in your diff.

ONE THING STILL OWED, AND IT IS NOT A REBASE TASK
A third reviewer found that OFFSET paging on the people list can duplicate or drop a row under concurrent
inserts (src/routes/people.queries.ts). I declined it deliberately: this branch touched that file only to add
the attendee population branch, and keyset paging changes the page contract for three API surfaces, the CLI's
--page, the UI pager, OpenAPI and the SKILL registry text. It needs its own ticket — #267 has the same defect.
Ticket minting is single-writer (CLAUDE.md), so intake must create it. Fix shape: keyset on (created_at, id);
ULIDs make it cheap; regression is read page 1, insert, read page 2, assert nothing lost and nothing duplicated.

ALSO NOT A DEFECT, DO NOT "FIX" IT
The session detail page renders the star count after the star button, which R2 forbids for the agenda chip.
The ratified v0.3 prototype does exactly this on the detail page, so changing it is a design ruling for the
operator, not a build fix.
